events.narrative: Numerous trees and wires were downed on Albany Avenue in West Hartford.
In Hartford, Milford Street at Homestead Avenue was flooded and impassable.

In West Hartford, Albany Avenue at Mohegan Drive was flooded and impassable. Cars were stuck in flash flood waters at King Philip Drive and Brewster Road.  There were reports of eight cars stuck in flash flood waters on Mohegan Drive near the intersection with Brewster Road, which was impassable.
In East Hartford, large branches were down on Birchwood and Milwood Roads.  A large branch was down at the the corner of Birchwood Road and Silver Lane.
In Enfield, power lines were down from wind on South Road at Phoenix Avenue.
In Burlington, a trained spotter reported an 8-inch diameter gray birch tree was snapped off about 3 feet above ground, approximately 25 feet long, blocking Woodhaven Drive.

Final snow totals ranged from 8 to 12 inches in southern Hartford County to 12 to 18 inches in northern Hartford County.  A trained spotter in North Granby, which had two heavy bands (one on the evening of the 1st and the other overnight on the 2nd/3rd) reported 18.0 inches.

In Windsor Locks at 404 PM EST. the ASOS at Bradley International Airport (KBDL) recorded a gust to 47 knots.  However, the Bradley Weather Contract Observer Supervisor estimated that a gust to 70 knots occurred within one-half mile of the ASOS.  A small brick wall just outside of the Signature b...

Snowfall ranged from 5 to 9 inches with the highest amount (9 inches) reported in Newington. The heavier snow (6-10 inches) fell in southeast Hartford county with less snow (3-6 inches) in the northwest of the county.

Snowfall generally ranged from 3 to 13 inches. The highest amounts were in eastern Hartford county with lesser amounts to the west. The highest report was 13.8 inches in Manchester. Winds gusted 30 to 40 mph.
In Hartford, a tree was downed, along with wires, on Holcomb Street.  Wires also were downed on Barbour Street.
In East Windsor, a tree and wires were down on Holcomb Terrace.  Report relayed by amateur radio.

In Wethersfield, multiple wires were down on Olney Road; large branches were down in a backyard on Clearfield Road; wires were down on Harold Street; multiple wires and a branch were down on Olney Road; a branch was down on wires on Church Street; and a branch was on top of the roof of a house on...
In Suffield, a tree fell on two cars on Barndoor Hills Drive.
In Windsor, a large tree was down on Stone Road.
In East Granby, the public reported street flooding with a road closure of an unspecified road a couple of miles south-southwest of the town center.
In Windham, at 824 PM EST, a 1 foot diameter tree was down on Plains Road.  Also, at 1043 PM EST, a tree fell onto a house on Oakwood Drive, per Fire Dept.
In Glastonbury at 445 AM EST, a tree was down on wires on Newell Lane.  Confirmed via photo on Twitter.
In Burlington, a tree was down on Rio Road.

In Avon at 550 AM EST, two 40-foot tall red pine trees were blow down on Irontree Court. In Wethersfield at 6 AM EST, a tree was down on Broad Street.  In East Hartford at 913 AM, the public reported tree branches down on Silver Lane at Oak Street near the Manchester line.  In Rockville at 1217 P...

Hartford County generally received 4 to 8 inches of snow.  Some specific amounts included:  8.0 inches in Granby; 7.0 inches in both North Canton and Simsbury; 6.8 inches in Bristol; 6.5 inches in East Windsor; 6.2 inches in Newington; 6.0 inches in Glastonbury; 5.9 inches a Bradley International...

Snowfall totals varied widely from as much as 18 in the northwest hills of Hartford county to as little as 1.5 inches in the southeast section of the county.  Some specific totals include - 18.0 in Granby/Hartland, 12.5 in Burlington, 7.2 Suffield, 5.1 in Bristol, 4.5 at Bradley International Air...
In Burlington, a tree and wires were down on Route 4 between Rt 179 and River Rd in Farmington.
In Rocky Hill, Main St was flooded from Dividend Rd to Elm St.
In Hartford, several cars were stuck in flood waters on Scarborough St.
In Suffield, Hale St at Taintor St was closed due to flooding.
In Rocky Hill, a large tree was uprooted, per picture on social media.  Time estimated by radar.
In Hartford, parts of Franlkin Ave were closed from 1 foot of water.
In Bristol, a portion of Rt 229 at Rt 72 was closed due to flooding.
In East Hartford, Brewer St was flooded with depth up to the wheel base of sedans.
In Southington, trees and wires were down across the road near East St at Kensington Rd.
In Enfield, Pearl St was flooded and impassable.
In Farmington, wires were down on Rt. 4 and New Britain Ave.
In Southington, the northbound lane of Rt 322 was flooded and impassable.
In Berlin, power lines were down partially blocking Mill Rd.
In Enfield, a tree and wires were down on School St and Nonotuck St.
In Bristol, there was a car stuck in floodwaters on King St.
In New Britain, there were downed power lines at the intersection of Hartford Rd and Stanley St.

Generally 3 to 17 inches of snow fell. There was a big gradient from southern Hartford county to the hills of northwest Hartford county. Some accumulations included 17 inches in North Granby, 13.2 inches in Hartland, 11 inches in Avon, 10.4 inches at Bradley Airport, and 8 inches in Southington.

Generally 3 to 17 inches of snow fell. There was a big gradient from southern Hartford county to the hills of northwest Hartford county. Some accumulations included 17 inches in North Granby, 13.2 inches in Hartland, 11 inches in Avon, 10.4 inches at Bradley Airport, and 8 inches in Southington.

Generally 4 to 11 inches of snow fell in Hartford County. This was the bullseye of the snow totals in southern New England. Some notable accumulations included 15.5 inches in Farmington, 15.2 inches in West Hartford, and 12.5 inches in East Windsor.
In East Windsor, there was a tree down near South Rd and Phelps Rd. There was a utility pole and wires down at Phelps Rd and Rt 5.
In Enfield, there was road flooding along Freshwater Blvd and Cranbrook Blvd that resulted in cars getting stuck.
In Avon, parts of Rt 44 had flooding with water covering the road.
In Southington, there were many reports of trees and wires down across town. There were unconfirmed reports of trees down on at least two homes.
At Bradley Airport the ASOS Station (KBDL) gusted to 77 mph.
In Plainville, a spotter reported widespread flooding in the area.
In Newington, a spotter measured a gust to 60 mph.
In West Hartford, there were multiple reports of trees and wires down including Timber Ln.
Damage was reported at the Simsbury Airport. A small plane was flipped up on its wings as well as damage to an airport hangar.
In Newington, there were several reports of flooding around town. Main St and Dowd St was flooded and impassable.
In Granby, a tree was down on Holcomb St.
In Canton, there were power lines down on Cherry Road.
In Farmington, strong wind gusts resulted in a few downed trees and large branches.
In Canton, there was water pouring into a basement through a hatchway.
A tree was down on wires and a tree was down on a house.
In East Windsor, two tree limbs about 4 inches in diameter were downed on Ellington Rd.
In New Britain, power lines and a tree were down through a house.

Winds generally gusted 40-50 mph but some gusts were higher including a 60 mph gust in Berlin at 12:46 PM EST. In South Windsor a tree came down on wires near the Manchester line. Generally 12 (lowlands) to 20 (high terrain) of inches fell with some of the highest totals being 21 inches in Simsbury and 20 inches in Bloomfield. Some of the lower amounts were 11.3 inches in West Hartford and 12.5 inches in Bristol.
Generally 9 to 12 inches of snow fell. Some of the highest reports included 17 inches in Marlborough and 16.5 inches in Burlington.
